text: 🇲🇽🎨 "Education is a right — not a privilege, not a competition, not a matter of meritocracy." — President Claudia Sheinbaum Two years in: 34 million students, over 20 million on well-being scholarships. The "Mi derecho, mi lugar" platform scraps entrance exams — 99.3% of applicants placed in one of their top three choices.

🇲🇽🏦 <u>MEXICAN BANKS HIT RECORD CAPITAL STRENGTH</u>

Mexico's banking system closed July with a capitalization index of 20.77% — its highest since the CNBV series began in 2010, and nearly double the 10.5% regulators demand, El Economista reports. Every single institution sat in Category I, the safest early-warning tier, and the banks cleared Banxico's stress tests for a severe adverse scenario. Record buffers — even as the Fed hikes and Washington rattles Mexican banks with sanctions threats.

🇲🇽🏘️ <u>CDMX SEIZES BUILDING TO REHOUSE EVICTED FAMILIES</u>

After roughly 70 residents were violently evicted from a building on Calle República de Cuba in the historic center in August 2025, Mexico City's government has expropriated the 636-m² property and handed it to the public housing institute (INVI) for social housing. "A historic act," said the families' lawyer Arturo Aparicio — the first time the capital has turned an illegal eviction, dressed up as a routine displacement, into public housing for the people thrown out.

🇲🇽✊ <u>ANGELA DAVIS GETS THE KEYS TO MEXICO CITY</u>

Angela Davis received the keys to Mexico City from head of government Clara Brugada, presenting her book "Abolición, feminismo, ¡Ahora!" at UNAM's international book fair. "Feminism has to be anti-colonial, anti-capitalist and anti-racist," Davis told the crowd, warning that women reaching power must "transform the world for all people," not merely make their own struggles visible. The Black liberation icon, once on the FBI's most-wanted list, honored in the capital of the Fourth Transformation.
banner: ANGELA DAVIS: KEYS TO MEXICO CITY

🇲🇽📊 <u>MEXICO'S 2027 BUDGET: WELFARE + INVESTMENT, NO NEW TAXES</u>

Mexico's 2027 budget pours 1.025 trillion pesos into Bienestar social programs and another 1.026 trillion into public investment — trains, energy, water — while trimming the deficit to 3.4% of GDP. Elderly pensions alone get 543.5 billion pesos; Benito Juárez scholarships, 190.6 billion. "No new taxes for the people, no gasolinazo," President Sheinbaum said — with tax revenue still projected to hit a record 15.9% of GDP, no new levies required.

🇲🇽💜 <u>UNAM OPENS MEXICO'S FIRST MENSTRUAL HEALTH CLINIC</u>

UNAM has opened the first Integral Menstrual Health Clinic at any Mexican university — free care for dysmenorrhea, chronic pelvic pain and heavy bleeding, staffed by doctors, nurses, nutritionists, psychologists and physiotherapists. "Dysmenorrhea is a public health problem of great relevance," said health-services director Gustavo Olaiz, noting that 70% of UNAM's students are women. Public education treating period pain as medicine — not as something to "normalize."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO MOVES TO OUTLAW "DRIP PRICING"</u>

Mexico's Congress is moving to kill "drip pricing" — the trick where an app flashes a cheap price, then piles on fees at checkout. A Morena reform to the Federal Consumer Protection Law would force delivery, ride-hailing and streaming platforms to show the "total and definitive price" from the first screen. Within days, the corporate lobby fired off letters to deputies demanding "working tables" to soften it — because transparency cuts into the margin.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Guanajuato Rides the AI Wave: $630M in Data Centers</u>

Guanajuato now hosts three data-center projects worth $630 million — two run by ODATA (Aligned Data Centers) in San Miguel de Allende and Apaseo el Grande — generating 200 direct jobs, plus a new $45-million, 60-MVA substation to power them. The state folded IT, AI and semiconductors into its "Guanajuato Suma" strategy, betting the reshuffle of global supply chains lands more high-tech capital in Mexico. (El Economista)

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Salinas Pliego's Reality-TV Land Grab Meets Garífuna Resistance</u>

Honduran police evicted a six-week "Camp for Life" so Mexican billionaire Ricardo Salinas Pliego's Grupo Salinas could film Survivor on the Garífuna beach of Uva de Cayos — blocking fishermen, cutting women off from water, and disrupting sea-turtle nesting. "A terrible repression is being fabricated. Once again they violate us," said Ofraneh coordinator Míriam Miranda — of the same tycoon fighting multi-billion-peso tax bills back home in Mexico.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Intelligence, Not Invasion: Mexico Captures a CJNG Regional Boss</u>

Federal and Michoacán forces captured Manuel Alejandro Rendón Aguilar, "Señor de la T," a CJNG regional coordinator linked to homicide, kidnapping, extortion and forced disappearance across five Michoacán municipalities. The security cabinet credited the arrest to "intelligence and investigation work" — coordinated surveillance between the SSPC, Sedena, Marina, the FGR and the state prosecutor.
